mechanism: Two-stage mechanism. Stage 1 (exact, identity-level, kernel-checkable): apply a Buchstab/Harman-style decomposition — an identity, no absolute values — to both C_{k,n} (all-plus prime-comb mass) and E_{k,n} (Mertens-weighted reciprocal-interval prime discrepancies), with the sieving base pinned to the wheel primes p ≤ p_k; the primorial wheel Q_k > 6·U_k makes the small-prime/zero-mode part exact (ρ_{k,n} < 1/6 already eliminates the zero frequency), so the Buchstab base carries no remainder. Iterate until every term is either an exact Type-I count or a terminal bilinear Type-II sum with both variables in [x^δ, x^{1−δ}]. Under hyperbola duality d ↔ q ≈ x/d, the reciprocal family is self-dual at d ~ √x, which is exactly the parity-critical Type-II scale m ~ x^{1/2} where the intervals (x/(d+1), x/d] degenerate to length < 1. Central claim: the factor 2 in H = C − 2E is the sieve parity factor — the parity-critical Type-II components of C and of 2E coincide term-by-term under the kernel-checked reindexation and cancel identically in H, not merely statistically. This is my proposed realization of the packet's hinted "exact transformation preserving the C − 2E correlation". Stage 2 (analytic): the survivor is a parity-neutral remainder R_{k,n}, and the Lean target is literally a windowed mean square — the Gram value equals the window path energy of the high source path (theorem sourceHighWindowEnergy_eq_projectedRenewalGramValue, CanonicalGapAncestryQuadraticClosure.lean:57), so the target reads Σ_{r<H} H(N+r)² ≤ C·H·N^{2+ε}. Close it by dispersion over the H consecutive square samples (gaps ~2N ~ 2√X, the √-scale intervals already built into the chain): expand the square; diagonal terms are pointwise sieve upper bounds; off-diagonal terms are pair correlations of primes in reciprocal intervals attached to two nearby square endpoints, bounded above by two-dimensional Selberg majorants (Montgomery–Vaughan style, singular-series main term plus constant-factor loss), whose main terms cancel against the mixed expected terms because the discrepancies are centered.
new_leverage: Three things a standard application would not have. (1) The parity-cancellation identity claim: reading the literal 2 in C − 2E as Selberg's parity factor and proving the parity-critical Type-II content cancels exactly is a structural claim about these specific coordinates, checkable in the kernel, not a generic tactic — it relocates the parity obstruction into one finite identity instead of an analytic estimate. (2) The wheel-exactness: within the synchronized block the Buchstab base over primes ≤ p_k has identically vanishing remainder (level of distribution is not estimated, it is exact), so no BV-type input is spent where sieves usually pay. (3) The dispersion family is native, not imported: the Lean Gram value is provably the window mean square over H square samples, so averaging over r < H is part of the target itself — this answers the usual "no family to average over" complaint without constructing one.
target_estimate: Named estimate, two parts. Part A (identity, target of proof): "Parity-critical cancellation identity" — for every synchronized block k and complete-square sample X_n, with decomposition parameter δ ∈ (0, 1/6), the Buchstab decompositions of C_{k,n} and 2·E_{k,n} restricted to bilinear range m ∈ [X_n^{1/2−δ}, X_n^{1/2+δ}] are equal exactly (integer identity under the kernel-checked reciprocal reindexation), so H_{k,n} = R_{k,n} with R containing no parity-critical component. Part B (dispersion, conditional analytic closure): for every ε > 0 there is C_ε ≥ 0 such that for all N, H with 1 ≤ H ≤ N, Σ_{r<H} R_{k,N+r}² ≤ C_ε · H · N^{2+ε}, i.e., RMS X^{1/2+ε/2} per sample, where the loss factors are: a multiplicative constant 4^J from J Buchstab iterations' Selberg pair majorants, and N^ε from divisor-function moments. Variables: k determined by N via block membership; δ fixed; J ≤ (1/δ)·log(1/δ). I commit that Part A is the theorem I would actually attempt to prove; Part B as stated is where the parity-neutral analytic content sits and is NOT provable by sieve upper bounds alone at exponent 1/2 (constant-factor loss on pair correlations is fatal at that strength) — sieves close Part B only at exponent 3/4-type strength unless an asymptotic (not upper-bound) pair-correlation input over the reciprocal family is supplied.

obstacle_positions.pinned_vs_averaged: Addressed at Type-I/base level: wheel exactness is pinned-native, the primorial start makes the base decomposition an identity with zero remainder, no exceptional-set averaging invoked. At Type-II/dispersion level: the only average is over the r < H window, which the Lean target itself contains, so no illegitimate averaging over starts; the residual uniformity needed is that Selberg pair majorants are pointwise-translation-uniform (Brun–Titchmarsh style), which is true but costs constants — flagged as a real cost, not a dodge.
obstacle_positions.large_sieve_non_transfer: Accepted; no modulus family is constructed. The angle's answer is that the H-window of square samples IS a family, and it is internal to the target (Gram value = window energy, verified in the Lean source). No off-diagonal-to-shared-modulus map is claimed; off-diagonal pairs are handled as prime pair-correlation upper bounds, which lose constants — this is exactly why the angle caps below rung 2 without an asymptotic pair input.
obstacle_positions.not_bombieri_vinogradov: Agreed and respected: the decomposition works through hyperbola duality on ordinary short intervals, never residue classes to varying moduli; no BV or level-of-distribution input is used anywhere (the wheel makes the only place it would be needed exact).
obstacle_positions.strong_induction_failure: The angle inserts no |M(d)| bound anywhere: Buchstab is an identity and all Mertens weights ride along signed until the terminal terms; cancellation across d is preserved by construction, consistent with the packet's demand. The failure mode it must still avoid: absolute values enter at the terminal Type-II majorant stage, but only on the parity-neutral remainder, after the claimed exact cancellation has removed the dominant correlated part.
obstacle_positions.parity: Front and center, and honestly: parity is relocated, not defeated. The claim is that C − 2E is precisely the parity-even combination (factor 2 = parity factor) whose parity-critical component vanishes identically. If true, the survivor is parity-neutral and sieve-treatable in principle, but sieve upper bounds still lose constants that cap unconditional strength near 3/4, so rung 2 additionally needs one genuine cancellation input at the critical scale. If false, the angle collapses to standard sieve limits (rung 0 only). This is the single load-bearing wager of the angle.
obstacle_positions.finite_range_deception: The positive claim (Part A) is a finite exact identity to be proven in the kernel, not an empirical exponent fit; numerics are used only in the kill test as a falsifier (an identity that fails numerically at one sample is dead), never as evidence of an asymptotic exponent.

kill_test: Compute exactly, for k = 4, 5 and a handful of complete-square samples X_n in each block (feasible at X up to ~10^7 since the packet reports C and E are already computed exactly in diagnostics): the Buchstab decompositions of C_{k,n} and 2·E_{k,n} restricted to the critical bilinear window m ∈ [X_n^{1/2−δ}, X_n^{1/2+δ}] with δ = 1/10. Test 1 (kills Part A): if the two restricted values are not exactly equal — not even after retuning the reindexation offsets — the parity-cancellation identity is false and the angle dies as stated. Test 2 (kills the weaker statistical fallback): if their ratio deviates from 1 by more than X_n^{-1/4} at several samples, even statistical cancellation at the needed strength is absent. This is a day of computation, not an asymptotic study.
rung0_plan: The rung-0 version is essentially a re-derivation of the elementary PNT in these coordinates, and the resonance is exact: Selberg's symmetry formula ψ(x)log x + Σ Λ(n)ψ(x/n) = 2x log x + O(x) is itself a factor-2 self-referential identity, and the elementary Erdős–Selberg bootstrap extracts o(x) from precisely such a C-minus-2E-shaped relation. Plan: run the same Buchstab decomposition with the wheel base, use only the trivial bound on the parity-critical terms (they are O(x/log x) in count after wheel pre-sieving), and close the window dispersion with Chebyshev-strength inputs to get Σ_{r<H} H(N+r)² = o(H·N²·(anything growing)), i.e., H_{k,n} = o(X_n) per sample on average — PNT strength, unconditional, with an explicit de la Vallée Poussin-type rate exp(−c√log X) if one imports the classical zero-free region through the E-side prime discrepancies. Every piece of the rung-2 machinery (wheel-exact base, signed decomposition, window dispersion) is exercised at rung 0 with only the terminal estimate weakened.
plausible_partial: Realistic at bounded effort, in order of confidence: (1) the kill-test computation itself, settling whether the parity-critical cancellation is exact, statistical, or absent — this is decisive information either way; (2) if the identity survives numerically, a paper-level (plausibly kernel-level, since the reindexation is already kernel-checked) proof of Part A, the parity-critical cancellation identity — a finite combinatorial statement; (3) the unconditional rung-0 theorem with explicit rate; (4) a clean conditional theorem: Part A plus an asymptotic pair-correlation-on-average hypothesis for primes in the reciprocal family over the square-sample window implies the full target at 1/2 + ε. I do NOT claim any unconditional fixed exponent θ < 1 is reachable: for this RH-equivalent object, any fixed θ < 1 almost certainly implies a zero-free strip, which is beyond sieve machinery; claiming rung 1 unconditionally would be dishonest from this lens.
self_assessed_risk: The assumption most likely to be false is the load-bearing one: that the factor 2 in C − 2E is structural (the parity factor) rather than an artifact of the centering/PNT-correction conventions, i.e., that the parity-critical Type-II components cancel exactly instead of merely being positively correlated as the diagnostics report. The packet says C and E are 'usually same-sign and positively correlated' — 'usually' is weaker than 'identically', and if the cancellation is only statistical with correlation bounded away from 1 at the critical scale, the surviving parity-critical mass is of the same order as the original problem and the angle reverts to rung 0. Secondary risk, stated plainly: even with Part A true, sieve pair-correlation upper bounds lose multiplicative constants that make the dispersion close only above exponent 1/2, so rung 2 requires importing one non-sieve cancellation estimate; the sieve lens alone ends at 'parity relocated into one checkable identity plus a conditional closure', not at RH.
